title: Multiplying 2-Digit by 2-Digit Numbers
seo_title: Grade 4 Multiplying 2-Digit by 2-Digit Numbers Worksheets (TEKS 4.4C, 4.4D, STAAR)
standard_text: 4.4C represent the product of 2 two-digit numbers using arrays, area models, or equations, including perfect squares through 15 by 15; 4.4D use strategies and algorithms, including the standard algorithm, to multiply up to a four-digit number by a one-digit number and to multiply a two-digit number by a two-digit number
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 multiplication worksheets for Texas TEKS 4.4C and 4.4D: 2-digit by 2-digit area models, partial products, perfect squares through 15 × 15, the standard algorithm and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Split both numbers and add the 4 partial products.
key_sub: 23 × 14 = 200 + 80 + 30 + 12 = 322. In the standard algorithm, write a 0 before multiplying by the tens digit.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Split both numbers into tens and ones. An area model has 4 parts: tens × tens, tens × ones, ones × tens and ones × ones.
  • Add the 4 partial products: 23 × 14 = 200 + 80 + 30 + 12 = 322.
  • In the standard algorithm, multiply by the ones, then by the tens (write a 0 first), then add.
  • A perfect square is a number times itself: 12 × 12 = 144.

Examples

Example

23 × 14 with an area model

20 × 10 = 200

20 × 4 = 80

3 × 10 = 30

3 × 4 = 12

200 + 80 + 30 + 12

Answer: 322

Example

36 × 25 with the standard algorithm

36 × 5 = 180

36 × 20 = 720

180 + 720

Answer: 900

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Multiplying only tens × tens and ones × ones: 23 × 14 = 200 + 12There are 4 partial products. Do not skip the middle two.
Forgetting the 0 when multiplying by the tens digitThe tens digit stands for tens: 36 × 20, not 36 × 2.
Adding partial products wronglyLine them up by place value before adding.

faq.a: You are multiplying by tens, so every product is a number of tens.

items.q: A café has 1,500 paper cups. It uses 6 packs of 185 cups this week. How many cups are left?
Ava says 47 × 23 = 235. Use an estimate. Is her answer reasonable?
items.e: 47 rounds to 50 and 23 rounds to 20, and 50 × 20 = 1,000. 235 is much too small, so the answer is not reasonable. The exact answer is 1,081; Ava forgot the zero in the second partial product.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 68 × 31?
items.e: Round both numbers to the nearest ten (70 and 30): 70 × 30 = 2,100. The exact answer, 2,108, is close to 2,100.

items.q: 26 students go to a science museum. A ticket costs $13. The teacher pays with $400. How much change does the teacher get?
Grace says 3,104 × 6 = 18,624. Use an estimate. Is her answer reasonable?
items.e: 3,104 rounds to 3,000, and 3,000 × 6 = 18,000. 18,624 is close to 18,000, so the answer is reasonable. (It is also exact: 3,104 × 6 = 18,624.)

items.q: A video game level has 449 coins. Harper plays it 5 times and collects every coin. How many coins does she collect?
items.e: Equal groups: 5 times × 449 coins, so multiply. Ones: 9 × 5 = 45. Write 5, regroup 4 tens. Tens: 4 × 5 + 4 = 24. Write 4, regroup 2 hundreds. Hundreds: 4 × 5 + 2 = 22. Write 22. Answer: 2,245.

items.q: A farmer plants 25 rows of corn with 57 plants in each row. How many corn plants are there?
items.e: Equal groups: 25 rows × 57 plants, so multiply. Step 1: multiply by the ones: 57 × 5 = 285. Step 2: multiply by the tens: 57 × 20 = 1,140 (write a 0 in the ones place, then 57 × 2 = 114). Step 3: add: 285 + 1,140 = 1,425.

items.q: A store has 32 packs of red markers and 18 packs of blue markers. Every pack has 12 markers. How many markers does the store have?
items.e: Step 1: packs in all: 32 + 18 = 50. Step 2: markers: 50 × 12 = 600. Or: 32 × 12 = 384 red and 18 × 12 = 216 blue, and 384 + 216 = 600.

items.q: Josiah puts 15 stamps on each page of an album. The album has 25 full pages. How many stamps are in the album?
items.e: Equal groups: 25 pages × 15 stamps, so multiply. Step 1: multiply by the ones: 15 × 5 = 75. Step 2: multiply by the tens: 15 × 20 = 300 (write a 0 in the ones place, then 15 × 2 = 30). Step 3: add: 75 + 300 = 375.

items.q: There are 36 eggs in each crate. A grocery store gets 24 crates. How many eggs is that?
items.e: Equal groups: 24 crates × 36 eggs, so multiply. Step 1: multiply by the ones: 36 × 4 = 144. Step 2: multiply by the tens: 36 × 20 = 720 (write a 0 in the ones place, then 36 × 2 = 72). Step 3: add: 144 + 720 = 864.

items.q: Caleb reads 25 pages a day for 14 days. His book has 420 pages. How many pages does he still have to read?
items.e: Step 1: pages read: 25 × 14 = 350. Step 2: pages left: 420 − 350 = 70.

items.q: Owen says 38 × 42 = 1,596. Use an estimate. Is his answer reasonable?
items.e: 38 rounds to 40 and 42 rounds to 40, and 40 × 40 = 1,600. 1,596 is close to 1,600, so the answer is reasonable. (It is also exact: 38 × 42 = 1,596.)

items.q: A pilot flies a route that is 1,996 miles long. She flies it 4 times this month. How many miles is that?
items.e: Equal groups: 4 trips × 1,996 miles, so multiply. Ones: 6 × 4 = 24. Write 4, regroup 2 tens. Tens: 9 × 4 + 2 = 38. Write 8, regroup 3 hundreds. Hundreds: 9 × 4 + 3 = 39. Write 9, regroup 3 thousands. Thousands: 1 × 4 + 3 = 7. Write 7. Answer: 7,984.

items.q: A new bike costs $366. A bike club buys 7 bikes. How much does the club pay?
items.e: Equal groups: 7 bikes × $366, so multiply. Ones: 6 × 7 = 42. Write 2, regroup 4 tens. Tens: 6 × 7 + 4 = 46. Write 6, regroup 4 hundreds. Hundreds: 3 × 7 + 4 = 25. Write 25. Answer: 2,562.

items.q: A factory packs 1,184 bottles each hour. How many bottles does it pack in 8 hours?
items.e: Equal groups: 8 hours × 1,184 bottles, so multiply. Ones: 4 × 8 = 32. Write 2, regroup 3 tens. Tens: 8 × 8 + 3 = 67. Write 7, regroup 6 hundreds. Hundreds: 1 × 8 + 6 = 14. Write 4, regroup 1 thousand. Thousands: 1 × 8 + 1 = 9. Write 9. Answer: 9,472.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 487 × 6?
items.e: Round 487 to the nearest hundred (500): 500 × 6 = 3,000. The exact answer, 2,922, is close to 3,000.

items.q: A school orders 26 boxes of pencils. Each box holds 36 pencils. How many pencils does the school order?
items.e: Equal groups: 26 boxes × 36 pencils, so multiply. Step 1: multiply by the ones: 36 × 6 = 216. Step 2: multiply by the tens: 36 × 20 = 720 (write a 0 in the ones place, then 36 × 2 = 72). Step 3: add: 216 + 720 = 936.

items.q: A theater has 24 rows of seats. Each row has 26 seats. How many seats are in the theater?
items.e: Equal groups: 24 rows × 26 seats, so multiply. Step 1: multiply by the ones: 26 × 4 = 104. Step 2: multiply by the tens: 26 × 20 = 520 (write a 0 in the ones place, then 26 × 2 = 52). Step 3: add: 104 + 520 = 624.

items.q: Gabriel swims 1,365 meters every day. How many meters does he swim in 6 days?
items.e: Equal groups: 6 days × 1,365 meters, so multiply. Ones: 5 × 6 = 30. Write 0, regroup 3 tens. Tens: 6 × 6 + 3 = 39. Write 9, regroup 3 hundreds. Hundreds: 3 × 6 + 3 = 21. Write 1, regroup 2 thousands. Thousands: 1 × 6 + 2 = 8. Write 8. Answer: 8,190.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 2,915 × 4?
items.e: Round 2,915 to the nearest thousand (3,000): 3,000 × 4 = 12,000. The exact answer, 11,660, is close to 12,000.
